draft.title: The cash rate
card: Banks lend money to each other overnight to manage their daily cash needs. The interest rate on these loans is called the cash rate.
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) sets a target for the cash rate. It changes the target at its meetings during the year.
Banks use the cash rate as a starting point for the rates they charge and pay customers. When it changes, their home loan and savings rates tend to change in the same direction.
Banks decide their own rates, so they may not pass on a change in full or at the same time.
draft.remember: The cash rate is the RBA's rate for overnight loans between banks, and other interest rates tend to follow it.

opts: The rate on overnight loans between banks
The rate banks charge on home loans
The rate banks pay on savings accounts
The rate the government pays on its debt
a.why: The cash rate is the interest rate on overnight loans between banks, and the RBA sets its target. Home loan and savings rates are different rates that tend to follow it, so they are not the cash rate itself.
a.clue: Think about who borrows and who lends at this rate.

b.q: The RBA lowers the cash rate. Mia has a home loan with a bank in Bendigo. What is most likely to happen to her loan rate?
opts: It tends to fall, though the bank decides by how much
It must fall by exactly the same amount at once
It stays the same, as the cash rate only affects banks
It tends to rise, as banks need to make up lost income
b.why: Home loan rates tend to follow the cash rate, so a cut usually leads to a lower rate for Mia. The bank sets its own rates, so it may not pass on the whole change or do it straight away. That is why the option saying it must fall by exactly the same amount is wrong.
b.clue: Banks tend to follow the cash rate, but they set their own rates.

a.best: The rate on overnight loans between banks

b.best: It tends to fall, though the bank decides by how much
